read.why: Reading correspondence, and filing it at triage, stays with the internal team (Nigel, 2026-09-19). Externals never pass: the architect was removed from request email reads on the same day.

send.why: Writing as the business is the directors' and the project manager's (Nigel, 2026-09-19). Free-form compose is tighter still — Admin, MD and FD alone (MailboxComposeRoles) — and this rule only says nothing may be WIDER than the four.

pagesWithoutARoleCheck./: the sign-in page, outside the session gate
pagesWithoutARoleCheck./login: the sign-in page, outside the session gate
pagesWithoutARoleCheck./set-password: an invite or reset token is the credential, outside the session gate
pagesWithoutARoleCheck./connect/authorize: the OAuth consent page: the caller is the scope
pagesWithoutARoleCheck./imagine/{Token}: the prospect's public door: the URL token is the credential, no session
pagesWithoutARoleCheck./privacy: the privacy notice: public by law, outside the session gate
pagesWithoutARoleCheck./my-day: retired: redirects to /dashboard, where the role home renders the worker's day
pagesWithoutARoleCheck./projects/{ProjectId}: redirects to the first project tab the role may open; renders nothing
pagesWithoutARoleCheck./projects/{ProjectId}/drawings: legacy address: redirects to /documents; renders nothing
pagesWithoutARoleCheck./projects/{ProjectId}/valuation-snapshot: legacy address: redirects to /valuation; renders nothing
pagesWithoutARoleCheck./projects/{ProjectId}/financials-setup: legacy address: redirects to /settings; renders nothing
pagesWithoutARoleCheck./projects/{ProjectId}/operations-setup: legacy address: redirects to /settings; renders nothing
pagesWithoutARoleCheck./projects/{ProjectId}/setup: legacy address: redirects to /settings; renders nothing
pagesWithoutARoleCheck./f/{Company}/{Slug}: a public form: open to anyone as it was on the JPS dashboard, a one-time link its own credential; no session
pagesWithoutARoleCheck./f/{Company}/pack/{Token}: a new starter's pack: the URL token is the credential, no session

Architect.why: P08 in the permissions matrix: the architect issues drawings and reads revisions. The extraction is the same drawing read as data, gated to DrawingReaders since 2026-09-19.
P08: the architect's instruction is their own instrument, and they sign off RFIs, submittals and variations.
P09 defects sign-off is the client's; the architect raises alongside them on close-out.

The per-role nav (2026-09-22): an architect's sidebar rows are project-scoped, so the project list admits the architect and answers with the projects that name their practice (ArchitectProjects), never the whole portfolio.

Client.why: P09: a variation is ultimately the client's instruction to spend, and defects sign-off is theirs. Scoped to their own projects by VariationOrderScope since 2026-09-19; the defect route is not yet.

Subcontractor.why: P10: a subcontractor reads drawing revisions for their assigned work. The extraction is the same drawing read as data, gated to DrawingReaders since 2026-09-19.
P10: the tender response is the subcontractor's own, and they raise and answer questions on the work.

_undeclaredOnPurpose.why: Left OUT of the lists above so the check keeps reporting them: an external role staging, sending or reading mail from the shared projects mailbox is an open question for the directors (permission check, 2026-09-19), not a settled rule.
